content.user_title: Protect Your Identity During Online Investigations
content.value_statement: Online investigations can expose researchers through accounts, networks, browser fingerprints, timing, and metadata. This skill provides threat modeling, compartmentation, persona controls, and exposure logging.
actual_capabilities: Builds a threat model based on observer capability, visible signals, and consequences.
Maps attribution risks across accounts, networks, browser fingerprints, timing, link previews, and metadata.
Provides setup, pre-action, and post-action checklists for research environments.
Compares VPN, residential proxy, Tor, and VPS tradeoffs for authorized investigations.
Grades collection exposure as clean, anonymous, pseudonymous, or attributed.
limitations: Does not verify current platform notification behavior or terms of service.
Does not provide legal advice or replace organizational authorization.
Cannot guarantee anonymity against platforms, network observers, or sophisticated targets.
Research personas may violate platform rules and create legal or ethical risk.

use_cases.title: Protect Sensitive Reporting
use_cases.description: Plan source research while limiting account, browser, network, and metadata exposure.

use_cases.title: Prepare Due Diligence
use_cases.description: Assess whether online collection could alert a company, executive, or monitored service.

use_cases.title: Control Case Attribution
use_cases.description: Document authorization, compartment research environments, and grade exposure after each collection action.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Exposure Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-action OPSEC checklist for researching public websites. Use only passive sources and identify what the subject could observe.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Proportionate Research Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare a normal browser, dedicated profile, and dedicated virtual machine for this authorized investigation: [describe case]. Recommend the least complex adequate setup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Selecting an environment based on case risk

prompt_templates.title: Assess Attribution Surfaces
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this collection plan: [plan]. Map account, IP, ASN, browser, TLS, timing, contact-graph, preview, and metadata exposure. Suggest safer passive alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Full OPSEC Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an authorized investigation OPSEC plan for [objective]. Include threat actors, consequences, compartmentation, legal review points, exposure grades, failure responses, and retirement criteria.

output_examples.input: Assess a public company website review from an office network.
output_examples.output: Risk: the company can associate the visit with the employer ASN. Use a dedicated browser profile and approved non-corporate egress. Grade the visit anonymous contact.

output_examples.input: Prepare to view a subject profile while signed into a personal account.
output_examples.output: Do not proceed. The platform may expose the viewer identity or create contact suggestions. Confirm current notification behavior using accounts you control.

output: Stop further collection from the exposed identity.
Record the identity, timestamp, action, and visible information.
Notify the case owner and reassess the collection plan.

best_practices: Document authorization, purpose, platform scope, and retirement criteria before creating any research account.
Prefer archives, registries, and other passive sources before contacting target-controlled infrastructure.
Log each exposure event immediately and notify the case owner when attribution occurs.
anti_patterns: Do not sign into personal accounts inside a research environment.
Do not use found credentials, password-reset flows, or false pretexts to access closed systems.
Do not impersonate real people or use research personas to elicit private information.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee anonymity?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify and reduce attribution risks, but platforms and sophisticated observers can still correlate activity.

faq.question: When is a research persona appropriate?
faq.answer: Only when authorized observation requires an account and legal, ethical, and platform-rule risks are documented.

faq.question: Should I use Tor for every investigation?
faq.answer: No. Tor can attract attention, trigger account challenges, and provide poor session stability. Choose egress based on the threat model.

faq.question: Is a private browser window enough?
faq.answer: No. It does not hide network identity, browser fingerprint, logged-in platform records, contact graphs, or external metadata.

faq.question: What should I do after accidental attribution?
faq.answer: Stop, record what was exposed and when, notify the case owner, and reassess the investigation plan.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal approval?
faq.answer: No. Obtain appropriate organizational and legal review for personas, platform terms, privacy obligations, and jurisdiction-specific restrictions.
